articles.title: AFP to Sara Duterte: Defending WPS is not picking fight with China
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said defending the country’s rights in the West Philippine Sea did not amount to picking a fight with China, following Vice…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said defending the country’s rights in the West Philippine Sea did not amount to picking a fight with China, following Vice President Sara Duterte’s call for the government to avoid confrontation with Beijing.

AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad (Reserve) said he agreed with Duterte that the Philippines should not antagonize other countries but stressed that asserting its maritime rights was a separate matter.

“Hindi po tayo nakikipag-away sa kahit sino mang bansa sa West Philippine Sea (We are not picking a fight with any country in the West Philippine Sea),” Trinidad said in a press briefing at Camp Aguinaldo, Quezon City.
“By merely standing up for what is rightfully and legally ours, we are not fighting any other country,” he added.

Trinidad was responding to Duterte’s remarks during a gathering with overseas Filipino workers in Hong Kong on Sunday, where she urged the government to maintain good relations with China despite the maritime dispute.

The vice president warned that deteriorating bilateral ties could threaten the jobs and businesses of Filipinos working in China. She also called for a team of diplomats and negotiators to handle the dispute rather than resorting to confrontations at sea or exchanges on social media.
Duterte further cited the disparity between the two countries’ military capabilities, arguing that the government should consider the consequences of confronting a more powerful neighbor.
Asked about her comparison of the Philippines’ military strength with China’s, Trinidad said the AFP would continue performing its mandate regardless of its capabilities.
“Hindi pinag-uusapan yung lakas ng sandatahan (It is not about military strength). We have what we have. We are improving our capabilities,” he said.

“Given what we have, we are good. Given more, we could perform even better. But it will not stop the AFP from fighting, from standing up, from supporting all our government officials who stand up for our rights in the West Philippine Sea.”
Trinidad also stressed that every Filipino, including elected officials, had a responsibility to defend the country’s national interests.
“The Arbitral Tribunal of 2016 is a legal landmark that upheld the maritime entitlements of the Philippines. Ito ay dapat ibandera ng bawat Pilipino (Every Filipino should champion this),” he said.
The 2016 arbitral ruling invalidated China’s sweeping maritime claims in the South China Sea, although Beijing has refused to recognize the decision.
Trinidad maintained that the Philippines had not instigated tensions in the disputed waters, citing China’s construction of artificial islands and its coercive actions against Philippine vessels.
He also ruled out scaling back military activities in the West Philippine Sea to accommodate diplomatic engagement with Beijing.
“Our RoRe (rotation and resupply) will continue, our patrols will continue, our MDAs (maritime domain awareness) will continue, our modernization program will continue,” he said.

Trinidad said diplomacy and defense were separate instruments of government policy, with the Department of Foreign Affairs responsible for diplomatic engagement and the Department of National Defense overseeing security matters. /jpv

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations are meeting in Abu Dhabi in a bid to end Europe's biggest conflict since World War II
Representatives from the EU are also to attend on the sidelines of the talks
The meeting comes as Moscow's invasion of Ukraine has dragged on for 56 months, killing thousands and displacing millions
Ukraine and Europe fear that the US could pressure Kyiv to make territorial concessions that are favorable to Moscow
Russia's state-owned TASS and RIA Novosti news agencies reported that talks would begin at 11:50 a.m. in Abu Dhabi (0750 GMT)

blocks.text: November 10, 2026
What demands are Russia and Ukraine likely to make?
Moscow and Kyiv have widely divergent demands regarding the conflict in Ukraine, which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of its neighbor in February 2022.

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its forces out of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, which are the regions that Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 without seizing all the territory they contain.
He also says Ukraine must give up its aspirations to join NATO, limit the size of its military capability and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church.
He has warned that he will use force to push through these demands if Kyiv refuses to accept them.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has ruled out yielding any territory that Russia has failed to take with military means.
He also refuses to accept any limits on the size of Ukraine's armed forces or restrictions on the alliances it strikes with Western partners.

articles.title: Author Jojo Moyes among UK travellers at risk of EU ban amid digital border system glitches
articles.summary: Errors in entry and exit records leave some Britons wrongly flagged as having overstayed post-Brexit 90-day limit

blocks.text: The writer Jojo Moyes is facing a two-year EU travel ban and €10,000 (£8,300) fine because of glitches with the bloc’s digital security controls.
She is one of a number of UK travellers who say their trips to the EU have not been properly recorded since the introduction of the EU digital entry and exit system (EES).
The system, which launched last year, has replaced passport stamps with biometrics recorded at border control in Schengen zone countries.
However, the botched rollout has led to some Britons being denied their post-Brexit right to spend 90 days out of 180 in Europe because the system falsely states they have used up their allowance.
Moyes, a bestselling novelist, was detained by French border guards after a holiday and accused of overstaying. She had spent only 23 days in the EU over six months.
She discovered that her departure from Portugal after a trip in May had not been logged on the system.

“The clock had been ticking ever since,” she told the consumer organisation Which? “The border control senior officer at Marseille warned me that I should not attempt to re-enter Europe until it is sorted out, or face a €10,000 fine and a two-year ban.”

blocks.caption: Jojo Moyes was detained by French border guards after a holiday and accused of overstaying. Photograph: Which

blocks.text: Over the summer, some countries suspended the EES and resorted to manual passport checks due to technical glitches and staff shortages. On Monday, it emerged that the EU is suing three firms over the failures.
The problem affects passengers whose biometrics were collected on their arrival in the EU, but not on their departure. In some cases, this means the system has failed to record that they have left.
The rolling 180-day window starts as soon as they enter the EU and, since Brexit, those who are deemed to have remained for more than 90 days face deportation or fines of up to €10,000.

Jane Nolan and her husband discovered that the EES wrongly showed them as having used up their 90-day travel allowance, preventing them from booking a trip to France. “We travelled to France in April by LeShuttle and spent 40 days there,” she said. “We have made no subsequent Schengen visits.

“We should have 50 days remaining, but the EU’s ‘check how long you can stay’ tool says: ‘Authorised stay: not OK,’ and zero remaining days. It does not show us which entry or exit record produced that result.”
The couple’s passports were manually stamped on their return to the UK in June as French authorities had suspended the EES to prevent long queues.
“We have asked the French authorities to check our records, but do not yet know what has gone wrong or whether the result could affect us at the border,” said Nolan.
In a case reported by the Telegraph a holidaymaker from the UK was detained at the Italian border and deported under police guard after a system error suggested she had overstayed in the EU.
Rory Boland, Editor of Which? Travel described the situation as unacceptable.

“This is one of the most serious in a long line of European border control failures,” he said. “The lack of care and accountability shown towards travellers, who risk being locked up and fines of thousands of pounds for rules they have not broken, is utterly indefensible.”
The Advantage Travel Partnership, which represents independent travel agents, said British travellers were being penalised for a chaotic system.

Its CEO, Julia Lo Bue-Said, said: “Travellers should not be penalised for failures in a system that is entirely outside their control. There needs to be greater accountability, alongside a straightforward process to challenge and correct inaccurate records.”

The Foreign Office said the problem was concerning. A spokesperson said: “We are aware of reports of inaccuracies in some EES records affecting British nationals, including incomplete records and the registration of some individuals who are exempt from EES. We are raising these issues as part of our engagement with the European Commission.”
It advised travellers to carry evidence of when they last left the EU and to raise any anomalies with border officials.
Travellers can check how many days of their allowance they have left by typing their passport number into the EES website. This records all visits to the Schengen zone since 10 April 2026.

If there is an unexpected shortfall, they can ask to have their record corrected before travelling by selecting the last country they visited on the Travel to Europe data protection page and contacting the relevant data controller.
Moyes said her efforts to do this have so far been in vain.

“In the last two weeks, I’ve tried every possible avenue,” she said. “I have now engaged an immigration lawyer, but not everyone is lucky enough to be able to afford this remedy. I have no idea how much time they think I have spent in Europe, and no idea whether I am safe to travel.”
The European Commission has been contacted for a comment.

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: The leaders of India and Ukraine spoke over the phone ahead of a new round of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States.
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said India was willing to help set up food corridors amid Black Sea attacks
India's Modi conveyed readiness to contribute to all efforts that are aimed at a peaceful resolution

blocks.text: November 10, 2026
Ukraine President Zelenskyy and Indian PM Modi speak ahead of Ukraine-Russia talks

India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy have held a telephonic conversation, with the Ukrainian leader saying that a discussion took place on Russia's attacks blocking grain exports in the Black Sea.
"India is ready to mediate in establishing corridors for grain exports in the Black Sea, blocked ​by Russian ⁠attacks," Zelenskyy wrote on X following the Monday evening call with Modi.
Modi and India's foreign ministry did not make a mention of the proposed food corridors in the official statements on the talks between the two leaders.
But Modi said he reiterated New Delhi's "firm commitment to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution."
India's diplomatic outreach in Ukraine war
In September, during a visit to Ukraine's capital Kyiv, Indian Foreign minister S Jaishankar offered to help end the Russia-Ukraine war.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha later said that his country had received four international truce proposals, including from India, which he described as the "most comprehensive."
Sybiha said Kyiv was ready to consider an energy and Black Sea ceasefire.
India's longstanding position on the Ukraine war has been that of a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy.
India has also continued its close economic relationship with decades-long partner Russia since the start of the war in 2022.
In October, Jaishankar first signalled that India had "got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy."

"We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, but going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them have on grain exports, on energy exports, on non-attack possibilities," he said at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi.
India also holds talks with Russia
Meanwhile, Monday's phone call between Zelenskyy and Modi came as negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States return to trilateral talks after months.
The fourth round of talks, starting Tuesday in United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi, comes after previous talks made no headway, with territorial and security guarantees being the major sticking points.
Zelenskyy said he had spoken to Modi about the latest diplomatic developments.
"The Prime Minister has said more than once, including directly to the Russian leader, ​that now is the time to end the war, not to continue it," ⁠Zelenskiy ​said, referring to the Indian leader.
Shortly after talks between Modi and Zelenskyy, Jaishankar announced that he spoke to the Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
"Our conversation focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives." the Indian foreign minister said.

WASHINGTON, USA – US President Donald Trump’s close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang came under renewed scrutiny on Monday, November 9, after the company said its board was investigating whether the tech executive has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Huang is one of Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates to at least 2025. Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support for the administration’s agenda and become a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market.
Advanced chips are the backbone of the US AI boom and government officials have previously tried to restrict China’s access to them through export controls to stifle its AI capabilities.

Nvidia’s board launched its probe after a New York Times report said Huang had a close relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who US intelligence officials believe passed information to the Chinese government. Nvidia shares closed down more than 4% on Monday.

blocks.caption: Nvidia, CEO Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy

blocks.text: “I’m pushing to investigate Jensen Huang and Nvidia to determine whether our national security was compromised,” said Senator Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, in a post on X. “We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration, who’s making these decisions, and who’s really got their hand on the wheel.”
Democrats on the House of Representatives Foreign Affairs Committee wrote to US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, calling on the Commerce Department to halt exports of advanced AI chips to China.

US Representatives Gabe Amo, Gregory Meeks and Sydney Kamlager-Dove sought answers by December 1 on whether top officials at the Commerce Department were aware of US intelligence linking Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based ⁠Megaspeed who is not related to the Nvidia CEO, to Chinese efforts to obtain Nvidia chips.
They also asked in their letter whether the top officials communicated with Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding Alice Huang and Megaspeed.

“If Commerce was not briefed, we need to know why. If it was briefed, we need to know how it responded. And if the Department knowingly permitted these exports despite credible national-security concerns, the American people deserve an explanation,” the letter added.
Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO, has a direct line to the US president. A Reuters reporter saw Huang’s full name pop up on Trump’s phone in December 2025.

Huang flew with Trump to China on Air Force One in May, the first visit by a US president to China in nearly a decade. Huang attended a high-profile state dinner in September for Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House. The company committed $25 million for Trump’s planned White House ballroom, according to media reports.

The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed on Huang’s relationship with the woman and on intelligence that she was giving information to the Chinese government, and that he chose not to act on the information.
The White House press office on Monday declined to comment further on Trump’s relationship with Huang.

Trump said on Monday the FBI was looking into the Nvidia CEO’s affair with the Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Trump said he had spoken to the CEO, who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy. Trump said he believed the CEO.
China’s foreign ministry said the spy accusations were “groundless.” Reuters could not determine Alice Huang’s location to seek comment from her on Monday.

Huang’s relationship with Trump has coincided with several favorable policy developments for the company. In April 2025, the administration backed off plans to restrict exports of certain Nvidia AI chips to China after Huang attended a dinner at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Florida.
In December 2025, Trump said the US would allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors, its second-best AI chips, to China and collect a 25% fee on such sales.

Trump has lavished Huang with praise, awarding him the nation’s highest honor for scientific achievement in October. The same day Trump gave Huang the award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million in Nvidia stock during the summer.
White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told Reuters at the time that third-party financial institutions independently manage the president’s portfolio. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: The US military evacuated aircraft from a second airbase in ⁠Britain on Monday after a threat from Iran, the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported, citing people familiar with the matter, weeks after Washington withdrew its bombers from ⁠RAF Fairford airbase over ⁠a suspected Iran-linked ​security incident.

Two US refuelling tankers that were using the RAF Mildenhall military base diverted to Germany earlier on Monday, while several other tankers at the base ⁠were moved to Germany and other locations later in the day, the WSJ report said.
The precise nature of the threat to RAF Mildenhall remains ⁠under discussion among US officials, it reported.
The US upgraded the security posture at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath, the report said, citing a US ‌official familiar with the ‌matter.

The posture was upgraded to Force Protection Condition (FPCON) Charlie, which is the second-highest defensive threat level in the US Department of Defense’s security system ‌and occurs when intelligence indicates that a form of terrorist action is likely.
“We do not routinely comment on the activity of other nations. Aircraft and other assets move regularly according to operational requirements,” a British Ministry of Defence spokesperson said.
A US Air Force spokesperson declined to provide the WSJ with details about the movement of assets, but said US aircraft rotate between installations and operating locations for a variety of ‌reasons.

Reuters could not immediately reach the US Air Force, while the White House, the Pentagon and the US European Command did not immediately respond to requests for comment ​sent outside regular business hours.
Five men were arrested outside RAF Fairford airbase in south-west England in September over a security incident with two others arrested later on suspicion of assisting Iranian intelligence.

The circumstances of the incident, which remain largely unexplained, attracted huge international attention, coming at a time of heightened concern about the security implications for western states ⁠of the war between the US and Iran, and prompted the US ​to remove its B-1 bombers ​from the Fairford airbase on security grounds.
RAF ​Fairford had been used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran.
British prime minister Andy Burnham said ‌last month that ​the activity at RAF Fairford ​was likely to have been coordinated in Iran.

While Tehran’s ambassador to Britain has denied accusations that it was involved in any plot against the airbase, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said in July that the Fairford base and any other base used to launch attacks against Iran were legitimate targets.

articles.title: Witness: VP Sara received P64,000 salary differential in 2023
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte received P64,194.72 from the Davao City government in January 2023 as payment for salary differentials dating back to her previous terms as mayor, a defense witness said…

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 2:39pm

Vice President Sara Duterte received P64,194.72 from the Davao City government in January 2023 as payment for salary differentials dating back to her previous terms as mayor, a defense witness said on Tuesday.
Davao City Accountant Vengeline Bahan testified on the 41st day of Duterte’s impeachment trial that the payment covered salary adjustments for 2020 and 2021.
Bahan confirmed a summary of payroll records showing that Duterte was due P64,194.72 in salary differentials.
“The particulars [in this summary of list of payroll] is salary differentials for the year 2020 and 2021 po,” Bahan said.
Salary differential refers to the additional pay an employee is entitled to receive after a salary adjustment is implemented retroactively, covering the difference between the old and adjusted rates.

In her testimony, Bahan explained that the amount given to Duterte covered January to December 2020 and January to December 2021, following adjustments under the fourth tranche of the Salary Standardization Law implemented in 2019.

Asked by defense counsel Lindon Bacquel why the payment was made only in January 2023, when Duterte was already vice president, Bahan said the supporting documents had been completed only at that time.
Duterte previously served as Davao City vice mayor from 2007 to 2010 and mayor from 2010 to 2013 and again from 2016 to 2022.

On Oct. 8, 2026, prosecution witness Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez, chief of staff of Bureau of Internal Revenue Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza, told the Senate impeachment court that Duterte's tax returns showed she had received compensation from the Davao City government in 2023.
The testimony then prompted private prosecutor Erwin Matib to raise constitutional restrictions on government officials receiving other compensation while in office.

Matib cited Section 13, Article VII of the Constitution, which prohibits the president, vice president and Cabinet members from holding other offices or employment during their tenure, subject to constitutional exceptions.

He also cited Section 6, Article VII, which provides that the president and vice president shall not receive any other emolument from the government or any other source during their tenure.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Samal assessor told to fix city's 'messy' records
articles.summary: Some senator-judges on Tuesday expressed "confusion" over the existence of two areas in the Island Garden City of Samal (IGACOS), where Vice President Sara Duterte had declared a property in her…

blocks.text: IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published November 10, 2026 2:21pm

Some senator-judges on Tuesday expressed "confusion" over the existence of two areas in the Island Garden City of Samal (IGACOS), where Vice President Sara Duterte had declared a property in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero admitted that he is confused as the deed of sale for Duterte’s Samal property and the field appraisal report of IGACOS city assessor indicated Barangay San Isidro, but the Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) noted that the property is in Barangay Matanos.
But city assessor Engr. John Kenneth Enumerables, a witness presented by the defense, said there no such thing as Barangay Matanos in IGACOS.
Senator Judges Risa Hontiveros and Erwin Tulfo also questioned the witness about the location of the subject property.
Escudero clarified that it was not Enumerables who mentioned Matanos, but the Vice President herself did in her SALN.

“To be fair to the witness, it was not the witness who used the name Matanos. It was the Vice President who indicated in her SALN the name of the barangay. The witness has been consistent in referring to the property identified earlier corresponding to TCT ending in 3134, as located in Barangay San Isidro, Kaputian District in IGACOS. He made no mention of Matanos,” the presiding officer said.

The defense witness also said he is unsure if the Samal property acquired by Atty. Manases Carpio, husband of Duterte, in 2013 was the same property declared in the Vice President’s joint SALN with her husband from 2015 onwards.

He confirmed before the impeachment court that the acquisition cost of the said Samal property as stated in the deed of sale is P3.45 million, not P4.04 million as stated in the joint SALN of Duterte and Carpio.
Senator-Judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson thus asked Enumerables to fix the city’s property records as it is quite confusing.

“Alam niyo kanina, gusto sana bumili ng lupa ni Senator Lapid sa Samal. Ayaw niya na raw kasi ang gulo ng record ninyo--may Barangay Matanos, wala palang Barangay Matanos. Tapos may San Isidro, ayon pala nasa Matanos,” Lacson quipped.

(You know, earlier, Senator Lapid wanted to purchase some land in Samal. But now, he decided not to because your records are quite confusing—there’s a mention of a Barangay Matanos, but it turns out no such barangay exists. Then there’s San Isidro, which, as it happens, is actually located within Barangay Matanos.)
“So paki-ayos niyo ‘yung record ninyo dahil medyo magulo,” he added.
(So, please fix your records, as they are quite disorganized.)
Enumerables said he would comply with the request of the senator-judge. –VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Here’s why Gary V recommends having at least one tomato-based meal per week
articles.summary: Del Monte and Gary V. encourage Filipino families to build a healthier routine with one tomato dish a week.

blocks.text: Del Monte and Gary V. encourage Filipino families to build a healthier routine with one tomato dish a week.

items: Gary Valenciano, known as 'Mr. Pure Energy,' is the new ambassador for Del Monte Tomatoes, promoting the Once A Week Habit advocacy for Filipino families to include tomato-based dishes in their meals.

Tomatoes are rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants like Lycopene, which can enhance cardiovascular health and reduce cancer risk, with cooked tomato products often providing greater health benefits.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by Del Monte Philippines and was produced by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the production of this piece.
Gary “Mr. Pure Energy” Valenciano is Del Monte Tomatoes’ newest ambassador, and for those who have followed his health journey, you already know why the pairing makes perfect sense.

Behind his remarkable stage presence is a man who has mastered the art of discipline when it comes to his health. Battling with Type 1 Diabetes since he was 14, surviving heart surgery, and overcoming cancer, Gary V. has consistently proven that his ‘Pure Energy’ is the result of conscious daily choices: from self-care routines to the food we use to fuel and nourish our bodies.
This time, Gary V. is supporting Del Monte Tomatoes’ Once A Week Habit advocacy, encouraging Filipino families to have one tomato-based dish at least once a week.

Incorporating tomato-based meals into our weekly meal planning isn’t much of a stretch for Filipinos, given how deeply embedded the fruit is in our culinary culture. We even have friendly online debates over the subtle differences between Afritada, Menudo, and Mechado, not to mention our love for the classic sweet Pinoy spaghetti.

Tomatoes are packed with essential vitamins and minerals, including Vitamin C, Potassium, and Vitamin K. But the real star is Lycopene, a powerful natural antioxidant linked to improved cardiovascular health, and reduced cancer risk.

What’s even more interesting is that cooked and processed tomato products like tomato sauce, paste, or ketchup can sometimes offer greater health benefits than fresh, raw tomatoes. Thermal cooking breaks down the fruit’s plant cell walls, releasing its bound nutrients and converting lycopene into a form our bodies can absorb much more efficiently.
Making conscious health choices

When asked about his favorite tomato-based dishes, Gary V. immediately mentioned Tacos and Arroz Ala Cubana. Like many Filipinos who find it hard to give up rice, his favorite twist is pairing Arroz Ala Cubana with shirataki rice, a swap that keeps his meal comforting yet still mindful.

Throughout his journey, Gary has relied on his four-spoke philosophy to guide his lifestyle: diet, medication, exercise, and faith. He then reframed his experience into a challenge for everyone, he shared: “If I can do it, what more [can] a person who has none of that baggage to carry?”

As someone who learns dance, I couldn’t resist squeezing in one question from Mr. Pure Energy himself: advice for people who are active, yet struggle to make healthier and more conscious choices due to demanding schedules.
“Sometimes…after dancing, they usually eat what’s available or easy.” He said. “Or sometimes, some of them are so conscious of their diet that they forget what they need.”
For Gary V., staying energized and healthy comes down to intentionality and research.

“What is your main objective? Is it just to burn fat? Is it just to sustain resistance and all? You can break it down, and from there, you can [start.] Go online and research what you would need in order for this to be maintained,” he said.

Learning more about lycopene and its health benefits only reinforced Gary’s belief that in order to perform better, you have to fuel your body better. “What you put into your body is what really matters. Since there are good options, put that into your body, and experience what the outcome will be.”
Having a healthy body does not happen overnight. It’s about building a habit of choosing what’s good for you and what nourishes you, like enjoying a tomato-based meal at least once a week.

Not Dela Paz, culinary category manager at Del Monte Philippines, also recommended exploring Del Monte Kitchenomics, an online recipe hub designed to help households prepare healthy, budget-friendly meals using Del Monte tomatoes and other Del Monte products.

“We really want to make it easy for Filipinos to adapt and to build this habit of serving tomato-based dishes at least once a week.” Dela Paz explained. “Kaya binibigyan rin namin sila ng different tomato-based options na pwede nilang lutuin once a week, para hindi lang [pang-ngayon] itong advocacy, but for their whole lifetime.” (That’s why we also provide them with different tomato-based options they can cook once a week, so that this advocacy isn’t just for today, but for their whole lifetime.)

Building healthy habits can still feel intimidating, especially when aiming for a better, healthier life for you and your family. But lifestyle decisions don’t need to be drastic. Just being that one person in your home who gently chooses better ingredients, researches healthy recipes, and introduces mindfully prepared meals can go a long way. – Rappler.com

articles.title: AFP on Sara Duterte's call: PH government not picking fights with China
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said the Philippine government is not picking fights with China amid tensions in the West Philippine Sea (WPS).

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 2:02pm
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said the Philippine government is not picking fights with China amid tensions in the West Philippine Sea (WPS).
This is in response to Vice President Sara Duterte’s call on the government to avoid provoking China.

“Yes, I support that statement na hindi tayo dapat nakikipag-away. Yun naman ang ginagawa ng ating gobyerno at ng bawat ahensya ng ating gobyerno,” AFP spokesperson for WPS Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said at a press briefing.
(Yes, I support that statement that we should not fight. That is what our government and every agency of our government is doing.)

“Hindi po tayo nakikipag-away sa kahit sino mang bansa sa WPS. Tayo lamang ay tumatayo sa ating karapatan na pinagkaloob ng Diyos sa atin, yung ating maritime entitlements, yung ating sovereignty and sovereign rights,” he added.
(We are not fighting with any country in the WPS. We are just standing up for our God-given rights, our maritime entitlements, our sovereignty and sovereign rights.)
Earlier, Duterte cautioned the Philippine government against picking fights with other countries, including China.

Speaking at a gathering with Filipino workers in Hong Kong on Sunday, Duterte suggested that resolving issues, such as the maritime dispute between China and the Philippines, is better handled through diplomatic talks rather than heated exchanges online.

“Alam ninyo dapat kasi hindi nakikipag-away ang gobyerno o ang opsiyal ng gobyerno sa kahit na anong bansa dahil napaka-complicated ng relasyon ng dalawang bansa. Hindi lang siya isang bagay lang, maraming aspeto ang relasyon ng Pilipinas sa bawat bansa,” Duterte said.

(The government or a government official should not pick a fight with any country because bilateral relations are very complicated. It is not just a single matter; there are many aspects to the Philippines' relationship with every nation.)
Trinidad said that the Philippines can pursue diplomacy while maintaining its defense posture. For Trinidad, every Filipino has a moral obligation to stand up for the Philippines’ national interest.
“The Arbitral Tribunal of 2016 is a legal landmark that upheld the maritime entitlements of the Philippines. Ito ay dapat ibandera ng bawat Pilipino,” he said.
On Sunday, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) also rebuked other Philippine government bodies and officials over their comments about China.
The DFA said these comments can undermine diplomatic efforts and that public officials must be aligned with the administration in its response.
"Under the Constitution, the President is the chief architect of Philippine foreign policy," the DFA said in a statement.

"Individual officials, agencies or sectors do not independently determine the direction of our international relations. Whatever personal convictions public officials may hold, their public platforms carry institutional responsibilities. They may not pursue preferred approaches toward China, or any other international partner, without regard for the consequences on the government's overall policy," it added.

Trinidad said that on the side of the AFP and the Department of National Defense (DND), they have a mandate to perform to secure the integrity of the national territory, protect sovereignty, and look after the welfare of the Filipino people.
According to him, the military will continue its efforts. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Australia to introduce mandatory reporting after OpenAI hack to combat artificial intelligence ‘going rogue’
articles.summary:
Government flags criminal law changes to ensure companies can’t argue in future ‘that someone didn’t know the computer was loaded’

  • Get our

blocks.text: OpenAI will not face criminal penalties over the Medicare data breach, but the prime minister has flagged changes to Australia’s criminal law to crack down on future breaches by artificial intelligence companies.

Anthony Albanese on Tuesday released the recommendations of a “rapid review” into the June breach of a Medicare statistics reporting service portal administered by Services Australia, but not the findings or the report itself, which he committed to releasing in the future.

A key recommendation is for the Attorney-General’s Department, Australian Federal Police and Department of Home Affairs to consider introducing “penalties for egregious regulatory non-compliance” and a “failure to prevent” offence, which would criminalise developing an AI model that engaged in harmful conduct while failing “to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm”.

The rapid review came in response to an AI agent, developed by OpenAI, accessing data from Services Australia and three other systems in June. The company did not notify the Australian government until mid-September despite becoming aware of the incident itself in August, prompting criticism from Labor and Albanese.
Guardian Australia revealed last month OpenAI used AI to help write the email to notify Australian authorities.
Albanese said the government would set up a new AI safety regulator and implement six key obligations on AI companies:

items: Maintaining security controls across all stages of development and deployment.
Identifying and managing serious risks associated with their models.
Providing mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian government rapidly.
Allowing independent evaluation of their models.
Maintaining and publishing safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management and transparency.
Responding to updated standards and rules as technologies change.

blocks.text: The review recommended the federal government “consider mandatory, time-bound AI safety reporting”, including around AI agents behaving in ways their creators may not have intended.

blocks.caption: Mandatory AI safety and security protections announced after OpenAI breach of Medicare – video

blocks.text: The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, appearing with Albanese, told reporters: “It should never be the case that there’s an argument that someone didn’t know the computer was loaded.
“We need to make sure that our laws and our systems keep pace with the technology and also make sure that we’re able to use the technology to find vulnerabilities before others do,” Burke said.
“The mandatory reporting, when artificial intelligence goes rogue, gives us a chance to be able to make sure that when this happens, the reporting occurs and occurs immediately.”

But despite the government’s earlier public anger at OpenAI, Albanese on Tuesday characterised OpenAI’s breach of Services Australia as “minor” in terms of the implications for personal privacy. Guardian Australia understands OpenAI is unlikely to face further legal proceedings related to the June breach.

While Albanese did not directly answer a question about whether the OpenAI incident in June would have breached the proposed new laws if they were in place, government sources indicated that the new legislation would address similar future incidents.
“The clear indication is that no information was got that involves people’s personal details,” Albanese said.
“All of that was confirmed essentially … but that doesn’t mean that it wasn’t a serious issue and that in other areas there might be more serious implications.”
after newsletter promotion
In a statement, an OpenAI spokesperson said the company was reviewing the recommendations and the government’s proposals.
“We have been in close dialogue with the Government and we’ll continue to engage constructively as it develops its proposed legislation,” they said.
A separate OpenAI-led process, which is discussing better coordination between AI developers and the government, is expected to report back by 31 December.
The review made 18 recommendations. Albanese said “we accept all of the recommendations and we’ve commenced work to implement them”.
The AI researcher Toby Walsh said the people in charge of these companies needed to be criminally liable to ensure they did the right thing.
“We’ve tried fining them, and we’re not the only ones. These companies are incredibly wealthy, and it’s almost impossible to fine them enough,” he told Guardian Australia.

But the Greens leader, David Shoebridge, branded the news a “capitulation” to the AI industry, claiming the reforms would not do enough to change the behaviour of those companies. He said the government should have committed to implementing even stronger changes, rather than the review’s recommendation that Labor simply “consider” them.
“Safety keeps coming second to corporate investment, and this review locks that priority in by tying every AI safety effort to bringing in more AI money and more datacentres,” Shoebridge claimed.

“Being a world leader in AI doesn’t mean being a doormat to big tech. It means being prepared to regulate it, to protect Australians and to make sure corporate profits don’t come at the expense of everyone else.”

The shadow home affairs minister, Jonno Duniam, said the Coalition backed the announcement, and had no criticism of the government. He said “AI is too important to become an unnecessarily partisan political contest”, signalling an “enduring and multi-partisan approach” to the technology.

articles.title: New Knesset speaker could be key to ousting Netanyahu as Israel’s PM
articles.summary:
Opposition politicians get first chance to take control of levers of power, even as they struggle to form government

Israel’s new Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday, giving opposition…
articles.byline: Emma Graham-Harrison Chief Middle East correspondent

blocks.text: Israel’s new Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday, giving opposition politicians their first chance to take control of some levers of power, even as they struggle to form a new government to unseat Benjamin Netanyahu.
High on the agenda will be replacing the speaker, who wields immense influence by controlling the legislature’s agenda. The role is currently held by Amir Ohana, a close ally of Netanyahu.
Gadi Eisenkot, the former Israeli military chief who got the presidential mandate to try to form a coalition government at the weekend, may take the role himself, Israeli media reported on Monday.

The effort to wrest away control of the Knesset is significant enough that more than 160 top former security officials, including heads of the military, intelligence and police, warned that rightwing activists were planning to disrupt the day with violent attacks.

“Actors who oppose replacing the Knesset speaker intend to go to the Knesset on the day of the swearing-in ceremony and to prevent the MKs and their family members from entering the building,” a forum of retired commanders, the Democracy’s Protective Wall, warned in a letter to serving security chiefs.
“These same actors are encouraging tens of thousands of citizens who support their stance to come and to help them with their mission,” Ma’ariv newspaper quoted the letter saying.
If Eisenkot does not take the speaker role, opposition parties have agreed that someone from his Yashar party will be the nominee.

The opposition parties hold 67 seats in the 120-seat legislature, enough to install a consensus choice for speaker. All have described the current prime minister as a threat to the state and are keen to start moving against him, despite divides blocking the formation of a coalition.

But several of the Jewish-Israeli opposition parties in his “change” bloc have sworn not to sit with the Palestinian-led parties that hold over a quarter of the bloc’s seats, or even join a minority government that has their backing.
Eisenkot has vowed to broker a national emergency government, promising to achieve it with “creative and unconventional political acts”.
In a sign of challenges ahead, he effectively warned that some election promises would have to be broken to unseat Netanyahu.
“No one will be able to fulfil all the [campaign] promises they made, and all of us will need to compromise. That is also leadership, to know when to decide and set priorities,” he said.
There have been protests across Israel urging Jewish-Israeli opposition parties to put unseating Netanyahu ahead of a racist commitment to excluding Palestinian-led parties from government.

Palestinian citizens of Israel make up about 20% of Israel’s population and voted in unprecedented numbers this year, giving them 19 seats. Without them, the opposition bloc has fewer seats than Netanyahu’s diminished coalition.

Rightwing opposition leader Avigdor Lieberman has been trying to seek an alternative path to government through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties. They have long been Netanyahu allies but have been frustrated by his failure to deliver on the promise to pass broad military draft exemptions for their community into law. Lieberman has campaigned hard for universal conscription, but appears to prefer compromise on this issue to working with Palestinians.
“Has the End of Times arrived?” leading Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) journalist Arye Erlich wrote in a column for Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper.

“Has Avigdor Lieberman … the biggest persecutor of Haredim Israeli politics has seen in decades, suddenly come to believe that he can compromise on a military draft bill and sit in a coalition government alongside the Haredim?”

Even if Eisenkot does broker a coalition deal, he may delay announcing it until Netanyahu’s speaker has been replaced. Netanyahu is a master of political survival and last-minute deals, fracturing past coalitions by luring defectors into his own alliance.
Ohana could delay signing in a new government for up to a week, and some of the opposition do not want to give Netanyahu that much time to attack the pressure points of any fragile deal.

If Eisenkot cannot form a government, the mandate is passed to other leaders and if they too fail Israel must hold elections again. In the meantime Netanyahu and his far-right allies would stay on as a caretaker government.
Although Netanyahu is calling for his opponents to join him in a unity government, a long period of limbo followed by a new vote offers him a likelier path back to power.
If an alternative government takes power, it will be harder for Netanyahu to destabilise it, said Gideon Rahat, chair in political science at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
“Once they establish a government, they might be a minority government, it might be hard for them to do things, but nevertheless, they will be governing and it would be hard to oust them.”

articles.title: EU manufacturers could give up on competing with China by 2030, warns commerce chief
articles.summary:
Jens Eskelund says Europe may need to allow its companies to become part of Chinese firms’ supply chains

Europe’s manufacturers could give up on attempting to compete with their Chinese…

blocks.text: Europe’s manufacturers could give up on attempting to compete with their Chinese counterparts by the end of the decade if current trends continue amid fears over mass job losses, the head of the European Union Chamber of Commerce in China has warned.

In a case of “if you can’t beat them, join them”, Jens Eskelund said European companies operating in China were now thinking “Made in China for China” could be replaced by a philosophy of “Made in China for the world”.

Eskelund, who heads the influential Beijing-headquartered body, said European manufacturers could find themselves at an existential crossroads by the end of the decade, asking themselves: “What is the point of trading?”

blocks.caption: The China import expo in Shanghai last week highlighted the latest five-year plan with the slogan: ‘New advances for a bright, win-win future’. Photograph: Xinhua/Shutterstock

blocks.text: As the EU gets tough with China with a deficit running at a record £1bn (€1.18bn) a day and an increasing mood for protectionism in Brussels, Berlin and Paris, he said European countries might need to shift their policies to allow domestic manufacturers to become part of Chinese firms’ supply chains, rather than treat them as competitors.

Eskelund, who is also a managing director of the shipping group Maersk’s Chinese operations, pointed to a report by Goldman Sachs that forecasted Chinese exports would lower the EU’s gross domestic product by 0.5% by the end of the decade while reducing Germany’s by up to 0.9%.
“It raises the question, if China’s trade delivers negative value, why trade?” the Danish businessman said.

blocks.caption: Jens Eskelund said European manufacturers could find themselves at an existential crossroads by the end of the decade. Photograph: Lisa O’Carroll

blocks.text: “If you are suddenly in a situation where trade creates a lot of value for one party, but it destroys value for the other, countries will begin to ask themselves, why do we trade?” he said, pointing to a potential doomsday scenario in which manufacturing disappeared from European countries, causing mass job losses, collapse in the tax base and potential multigenerational unemployment and spiralling social benefits costs.
Speaking in Brussels, where he has been in back-to-back meetings with European Commission officials to give them feedback from Beijing, he said Europe is at an inflection point.
“If we create new dependencies, ultimately that might result in Europe losing its ability to determine its own future,” with mass job losses and fraying of communities, Eskelund added.

That existential threat is already beginning to bite in Europe’s car, chemicals and renewable energy sectors, with the German automotive industry hit by a double whammy of reduced profits in China and cheap competition at home from Chinese companies such as BYD, Geely and SAIC Motor. Last week, BMW said its sales in China had dropped 22% in the first nine months of the year, in line with expectations of suppressed domestic demand, while issuing a second profit warning this year.

blocks.caption: Visitors watch a humanoid robot band perform at an expo in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province. Photograph: Costfoto/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Eskelund is not a fan of the term “China shock 2.0” – which refers to the impact of the huge rise in exports of, cars, chemicals and components – on local industry to the EU in the last five years. He said it should not have come as a surprise as Beijing’s plans to displace imports were the enduring theme of the last three five-year plans since Beijing’s Made in China strategy was agreed in 2015.

“I don’t really like the term China shock 2.0 because these things that are happening should not be a shock because it is all written in their five-year plans so you should be able to anticipate that,” Eskelund said.
“The proof of concept here is that China has been laser-focused on reducing its own dependencies over the last 30 years,” he added, pointing to a concomitant reduction in imports.

A recent report by Centre for European Reform (CER) urged Germany to stop “admiring” Beijing and change its strategy, with China’s latest five-year plan (2026 to 2030) a doubling-down on “self-reliance”.
“It is committed to displacing imports in the few sectors where it still depends on foreign supply,” said the CER.

blocks.caption: Workers paint wind turbine blades at a factory of Guodian United Power in Baoding, Hebei province. Photograph: Alexander F Yuan/AP

blocks.text: The sectors that have been identified in China’s latest five-year plan are AI, quantum computing; robotics; smart and green tech; biomanufacturing; brain-computer interfaces; and 6G communications.
Solar panels, wind turbines, robots, driverless cars, advanced chips are part of China’s new strategy for global domination.

Eskelund’s advice to those industries in Europe is not to hide but brace themselves for China to deliver. Once a strategy is decided in Beijing, incentives, tax breaksand subsidies flow down by region to town and village levels. Officials across the country know what to focus on and do, he said.
after newsletter promotion
His advice to EU leaders: “Engage with China and discuss getting to a point where everyone can see value is being created for both sides”, something he thinks Beijing understands.
While this might be an obvious point, Eskelund said a fundamental shift in approach was needed in Europe.

“China has always been very focused on outcomes, whereas Europe has been more focused on principles. It raises the question of whether following principles is delivering undesirable outcomes,” Eskelund said.

A view expressed in some quarters, including the UK, that trade imbalance could be addressed by increasing exports was just “fantasy”, said Eskelund, with this year’s surplus against the rest of the world expected to surpass 2025’s record $1.2tn (£900bn).

Eskelund said many companies were still making good money in China but the brutal competition in the country’s supply chains, combined with a currency undervalued by about 30%, left Europeans in the dust.
“What we see right now is that in almost all industrial verticals, almost anywhere in the world, you would have one and probably several Chinese competitors” he said.
“It’s just very, very difficult in most industries to compete with the Chinese.”

blocks.caption: An e-commerce warehouse in Jinhua City,  Zhejiang province.  Photograph: REX/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Giving up on trade is not the answer. If you can’t beat them join them. And that is what is now happening, the chamber has found.
“One way that they can compete with the Chinese supply chain is to become a part of the Chinese supply chain itself,” Eskelund said.
“For many companies it’s not the profit that you make in China that matters as much as the way Chinese supply chains enable you to compete on a global marketplace.”
This could mean making the products in China in joint domestic partnerships with European companies and getting into global supply chains in conjunction with Chinese firms.

“It is a sort of evolution from the old days when you came to China to service the Chinese market in China for China. It has now become: be in China, for the world. I think it’s a fairly significant shift,” Eskelund said.
For many of his members this had led to an “uptick in confidence” in the past year.
“This has turned out to be one of the ways that companies adapt, faced with a saturated market in China, they begin to explore exports,” he said.

articles.title: Young people in UK hit by ‘low-gear economy’, warns Bank of England deputy
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Iran war has fuelled energy price rise and clouded outlook, driving up unemployment, says Clare Lombardelli

Young people in Britain are bearing the brunt of a “low-gear economy”…

blocks.text: Young people in Britain are bearing the brunt of a “low-gear economy” as employers hold back from hiring amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East, a deputy governor of the Bank of England has warned.

Clare Lombardelli, the Bank’s deputy governor for monetary policy, said the unfolding conflict, which has triggered a surge in energy prices and clouded the outlook for the economy, was contributing to an increase in youth unemployment.
“What you see is the cost falling on young people, so you can see this rapid rise in the number of young people who are struggling to find jobs,” she said.

Against a highly volatile backdrop, she also warned Threadneedle Street was preparing for a “live” decision on interest rates next month after it increased the cost of borrowing last week for the first time in three years.
In an interview with the Guardian, Lombardelli said the UK’s employers were attempting to navigate the complex geopolitical backdrop by holding on to staff and freezing new recruitment.

“It’s what I call a low-gear economy. So a labour market where you’re seeing a real fall-off in hiring. But actually, we’re not seeing much in the way of redundancies. What’s going on is this kind of low hire, low fire dynamic,” she said.
“They [employers] are delaying hiring. They want to see if this uncertainty is going to resolve – like all of us. None of us thought we’d be nine months into this conflict.
“If firms are not hiring, obviously, by definition, that means people that are new to the labour market are hurt by that.”

Her comments come as Andy Burnham’s government awaits the findings of a report into young people and work by the former Labour cabinet minister, Alan Milburn, which is expected to be published next week.

With employers facing rising costs triggered by the Iran war, higher taxes and weaker levels of demand from consumers squeezed by the cost of living crisis, unemployment in the UK has risen this year to 4.7%. Youth unemployment has risen at a sharper rate to the highest levels outside the Covid pandemic since 2015.

Tackling the UK’s youth jobs crisis is also a growing priority for the government after an increase in the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) to almost a million.

blocks.caption: Lombardelli is a former Treasury and OECD economist. Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian

blocks.text: Lombardelli is expected to outline her concerns over a slowdown in labour market dynamism at a speech in London on Tuesday.

Lombardelli joined the majority of the Bank’s monetary policy committee (MPC) in voting to lift the base rate from 3.75% to 4%. She said a further quarter-point rise could be warranted from as early as its next policy meeting in December.
“Every meeting is live for us. December is, you know, it’s certainly plausible. What’s the market pricing at the moment? It’s about 50/50 for December,” she said.
after newsletter promotion

“I think it depends what we see on the conflict and the energy prices and it depends what we see in the wider data and how all that fits together. But I wouldn’t rule it out. Equally, I don’t have enough information just yet.”

Lombardelli was among members of the MPC who joined the Bank’s governor, Andrew Bailey, in raising the prospect of another rate rise in the near future – with a resolution to the Iran conflict the key factor that will influence the decision.

Oil prices have fallen sharply, to below $100 a barrel, after the Democrats’ victories in the US Congress, which some investors have interpreted as potentially constraining Donald Trump’s capacity to prolong the conflict in Iran. Trump said at the weekend that he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progressed.

Lombardelli, a former Treasury and OECD economist, said the impact of an increasingly stagnant jobs market was being seen particularly in sectors that offer young people their first job. “So that might be hospitality, it might be retail, in particular,” she said. “If you look at the distribution of where variances are, they’ve really fallen off in those sectors where young people can get their first start in the labour market.”
She added that employers surveyed by the Bank suggested there is “a sense that hiring a young person is a higher risk than it used to be”.

Threadneedle Street is focusing heavily on the jobs market amid concerns that current high levels of inflation could become entrenched in the economy if workers have enough bargaining power to push for higher wage settlements – which could lead companies to put up their prices to cover higher wage bills, stoking inflation. Signs of a weaker labour market could diminish this risk.

However, Lombardelli said that higher levels of unemployment would not necessarily bear down on inflationary pressures. This is because employers – holding on to the staff they needed – were only hiring for positions they found harder to fill.
“You can have higher unemployment without it exerting a downward pressure on inflation,” she said. “So that’s obviously a problem.”

articles.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
articles.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

image.caption: Fast food is typically calorie-rich, but low in nutritional valueImage: Christoph Schmidt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).
The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.

"In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," said Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president. "You could have a severe vitamin D deficiency for months before any symptoms appear at all. The same applies for vitamin B12. By the time symptoms appear, such as nerve damage, it's already too late."

A long-term B12 deficiency can damage the spinal cord, leading to numbness in the limbs, muscle weakness or even paralysis. Less common deficiency-related brain damage can cause memory loss and mental health issues.
Undernutrition vs. malnutrition
All B vitamins play an important role in metabolism, blood formation and healthy nerve function.

Vitamins, along with various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, iron, iodine and zinc, are classed as micronutrients. The body needs to source them from food, as it cannot produce them itself. Our bodies also need macronutrients like carbohydrates, carbohydrates, protein and fats that provide us with energy.

If the body consumes less food than it needs to maintain all bodily functions over a prolonged period of time, then this is known as undernutrition. A recent World Food Organization (FAO) report estimates that approximately 645 million people worldwide suffer from chronic undernutrition.

Malnutrition, on the other hand, occurs when we consume enough calories but lack certain macronutrients or micronutrients in our food. This, too, can make one sick over time and even prove fatal. About 2 billion people worldwide suffer from this so-called hidden hunger, most of them in the Global South. That said, even some people in industrialized nations lack important micronutrients in their nutrition.

blocks.caption: Golden rice, seen left, is genetically engineered to combat vitamin A deficiencyImage: Universität Freiburg/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: One study, for instance, found that just under three-quarters of the US population did not meet the recommended daily intake of vitamin D between 2007 and 2010, with more than two-thirds falling short of the recommended amount of vitamin E. And in Germany, about one-third of the population suffered from vitamin D deficiency in 2017, according to the German Nutrition Society. Such deficiency can cause bone, joint and muscle pain. It may also lead to an increased risk of falls and bone fractures.

About one-third of Germans also had an insufficient intake of iodine, a trace element that is indispensable for the production of thyroid hormones. Iodine deficiency can therefore disrupt normal thyroid function. Not only that — during pregnancy, a baby's brain and nervous system can only properly develop with an adequate supply of iodine.

The cultivation of agricultural produce with partially long shelf life or high yields has in some cases caused a decrease in the micronutrient content of fruits, vegetables and grains. Whether this drop in micronutrients is impacting human health, however, is a matter of debate.
Empty calories

Malnutrition can result from an unbalanced diet that, while filling and providing energy, lacks essential micronutrients. Examples of such empty calories include fast food and highly processed foods, as well as white bread and white rice.
Poverty is often the reason for such an unbalanced diet, for example when people in the Global South can only afford to buy staples such as flour or rice.
Another study found that in Germany, households at risk of poverty are more likely to consume foods that are low in nutrients and high in calories.

Depression is also associated with an increased risk of nutrient deficiency. "People often lose their appetite, and when they neglect their self-care, they may end up eating a very unbalanced diet," Pirlich told DW. His research shows that older adults and people who live alone often develop malnutrition, too. The risk also increases the more medications a person takes.

Many diseases result in the body being less efficient at absorbing or utilizing nutrients through the intestines. This applies to people with inflammatory or chronic disease, such as Crohn's disease, celiac disease, liver disease and cancer.
Malnutrition and hospital care

The DGEM estimates that some 30% of all patients receiving inpatient care in Germany are affected by or at risk of malnutrition. Yet health insurance data shows that only about 1% of patients are screened and treated for nutrient deficiencies.

Often, patients' malnutrition worsens during their hospital stay. The consequences can be serious, potentially causing additional complications, delayed recuperation, longer hospital stays and even increased mortality rates. This results in higher healthcare expenditure, amounting to billions each year.

German policymakers and medical associations are therefore developing a plan to better screen for and treat malnutrition in hospitals. The road map will be ready by 2027 and copy the Dutch approach in the sense that all patients are checked for nutritional deficiencies upon hospital admission.

blocks.caption: Elderly people are at higher risk of malnutritionImage: Karl-Josef Hildenbrand/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: How can we avoid nutrient deficiency?
Pirlich wants to see such screenings for at-risk groups in outpatient clinics, too: "This includes all those with chronic and serious illnesses and, above all, older adults."
To prevent poverty-related malnutrition, Pirlich suggests increased access to healthy food, offering free school meals as an example.

The nutritional expert recommends eating a diet that is varied and largely plant-based. "Secondary plant compounds have a very positive effect, and if you eat a highly diverse diet, you consume many different foods that are [nutritionally] beneficial," said Pirlich.
There's a simple rule of thumb: The more colorful your food, the better.

Also, cook vegetables as gently as possible, because overheating and keeping them warm for too long destroys their vitamins. Long storage periods also lead to vitamin loss, so it makes sense to go for seasonal and regional foods in particular.
But even when ensuring a healthy and balanced diet, some people still develop a nutrient deficiency. A blood test can provide clarity, and dietary supplements may help make up for the deficiency.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: After Typhoon Samuel’s exit, Philippines likely storm-free in coming days
articles.summary: The northeast monsoon is affecting Luzon on Tuesday, November 10, while the easterlies are affecting the rest of the country

blocks.text: SAMUEL. Satellite image of Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka) outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility as of November 10, 2026, 8 am.
PAGASA
The northeast monsoon is affecting Luzon on Tuesday, November 10, while the easterlies are affecting the rest of the country

items: Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka) left the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Monday, November 9, and no other potential tropical cyclones are being monitored.
The northeast monsoon and the easterlies are causing rain in parts of the country on Tuesday, November 10.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – New tropical cyclones are less likely to develop within or enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) in the next two weeks or so, following the swift exit of Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka).
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said Samuel left PAR at 4 pm on Monday, November 9, just hours after its entry at 8:40 am.
It was the Philippines’ 19th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the first for November, but stayed far from land and had no impact on the country.
As of 8 am on Tuesday, November 10, Samuel was already 1,720 kilometers east northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, moving east northeast or away from PAR at 25 kilometers per hour (km/h).

At the time of its exit from PAR on Monday afternoon, the typhoon had maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h. It has since strengthened, with its maximum sustained winds reaching 155 km/h on Tuesday morning. Its gustiness is now up to 190 km/h.
On Tuesday, the northeast monsoon or amihan is affecting Luzon, while the easterlies or warm winds from the Pacific Ocean are affecting the rest of the country.

The northeast monsoon may cause moderate to at times heavy rain in Aurora, Quezon, and Camarines Norte; light rain in Cagayan Valley and the Cordillera Administrative Region; and isolated light rain in the rest of Luzon.

The easterlies are bringing scattered rain and thunderstorms to Eastern Samar, Southern Leyte, Bohol, Caraga, the Davao Region, Misamis Oriental, and Camiguin, as well as isolated rain showers or thunderstorms to the rest of the Visayas and the rest of Mindanao.
The current presence of El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean does not mean there will be no rainfall in the Philippines or zero tropical cyclones inside PAR.

El Niño only leads to reduced rain, and tropical cyclones can still enter PAR. Tropical cyclones could be fewer, but they may still reach typhoon or even super typhoon status during El Niño. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Samal City assessor unsure if Mans Carpio property listed in Sara Duterte's joint SALN
articles.summary: A defense witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte said Tuesday he was unsure if the Samal property acquired by the latter's husband in 2013 was the same property declared in…

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 1:40pm

A defense witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte said Tuesday he was unsure if the Samal property acquired by the latter's husband in 2013 was the same property declared in their joint Statement of Assets and Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) from 2015 onwards.

Engineer John Kenneth Enumerables, assessor of the Island Garden City of Samal, made the response when asked by private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa, Jr. during the cross examination on Day 41 of Duterte's impeachment trial.

Tolosa asked Enumerables if the Samal property under the Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) 142-2019013134 is the same property indicated in the Vice President's SALN, to which Enumerables replied, "I'm not certain, Sir."

At the same time, Enumerables confirmed before the Senate impeachment court that the acquisition cost of the said Samal property as stated in the Deed of Sale is P3.45 million, not P4.04 million as stated in the joint SALN of the Vice President and her husband, lawyer Manases "Mans" Carpio.
Asked by Tolosa if the Samal property under the said TCT 142-2019013134 did not contain an annotation of contract to sell, Enumerables answered, "Correct, Sir."

Before making this statement, Enumerables said the Samal property, as indicated in the TCT 142-201901334, is the same property listed in the vice president's SALN "based on market value and assessed value" worth P346,960 and P4.9 million, respectively.

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero asked Enumerables if the latter has other basis for concluding that the Samal property listed in the SALN and under TCT 142-201901334 are one and the same, instead of comparing it with the market value and assessed value.
Enumerables said he does not have any.
"Wala po, your honor. Kasi hindi po nakalagay ang title number," Enumerables said.
(I don't have anything other than that. Because the title number is not indicated [in the SALN].)
Escudero said Enumerables' answer was understandable because the SALN does not require the title number anyway.
The prosecution argues that the said P3.4-million Samal property as indicated in the Deed of Sale was not declared by Duterte in her SALN.

The defense, however, contends that P4.04-million Samal property indicated in the SALN of the Vice President is one and the same with the P3.4-million Samal property being referred to by the prosecution.

The impeachment case against the Vice President rests solely on Article 2, which pertain to betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution for accumulating unexplained wealth of P817 million to as much as P1.5 billion due to non-full declaration of assets and non-divestment of business. — VDV, GMA News
